q: 1. Pay Back period is counted only after ......
options: starting of the construction of a project
completion of the construction of project
explain: Benefits begin only when the project is commissioned, so the payback period is counted from commissioning, not from tendering or construction.

q: 2. For the selection of any project the NPV should be ......
explain: A project is acceptable if NPV is zero or more; the minimum acceptable NPV is 0. A negative NPV is rejected, so option b cannot be right.

q: 3. The difference of discounted benefit and cost is called ......
explain: NPV = present value of benefits minus present value of costs.

q: 4. As the present worth of the project increases the project becomes more feasible ......
explain: Higher present worth means greater net economic gain, so the project is more feasible economically.

q: 5. For the selection of any project minimum future worth should be ......
explain: Future worth must be zero or positive for acceptance, so the minimum is 0.

q: 6. Project is assumed as feasible if ......
options: IRR is greater than borrow rate
IRR is lesser than borrow rate
IRR is equal to borrow rate
explain: A project is feasible when its IRR exceeds the cost of borrowing.

q: 7. In a project selection, minimum B/C ratio should be
explain: The decision threshold is exactly 1.

q: 8. For the selection of any project which one is mostly used ......
explain: The key marks IRR as the most widely used criterion. Note: many textbooks name NPV; follow the key.

q: 9. The number of years required for the net operating benefits to payback the initial cost of the project is called
explain: This is the definition of the payback period — the time needed for net benefits to equal the initial investment.

q: 10. During analysis of any project, numerical value of net present worth is found negative then, internal rate of return should be ......
explain: A negative NPW at a trial rate means the IRR is lower than that rate, so a lower discount rate must be tried. The key marks a.

q: 11. MARR (Marginal Annual Rate of Return) is
explain: MARR is the minimum acceptable return an investor expects after committing capital.

q: 12. The numerical value of MARR is
explain: For a project to be accepted, the Internal Rate of Return (IRR) must exceed the MARR.

q: 13. MARR (Marginal annual rate of return) is
explain: MARR represents the minimum acceptable rate of return expected as benefit resulting after an investment is made (note: options a and b are printed identically in the source book).

q: 14. The benefit cost ratio is ......
options: superior to all of the above method
explain: A higher discount rate lowers the present worth of future benefits more than costs, so B/C falls as the discount rate rises.

q: 15. The discount rate that makes the net present value equal to zero is known as ......
explain: IRR is the discount rate at which NPV = 0.

q: 16. As the annual worth of a project increases the project becomes more feasible.
explain: Similar to NPV, a higher Annual Worth (AW) indicates better economic returns over the project life.

q: 17. Internal rate of return should be
explain: For a project to be profitable, the IRR (the project's yield) must be higher than the cost of capital or borrowing rate.

q: 18. For the selection of any project, which one is mostly used?
explain: While others are used, NPV is often considered the most reliable metric for maximizing shareholder wealth in financial theory.

q: 19. Which of the following has least significance in Benefit cost Analysis of a public project?
options: identification of relevant benefits and costs
measurement of the benefits and costs
explain: In benefit-cost analysis of public projects, payback period is of least significance compared to properly identifying, measuring, and handling uncertainty in benefits and costs.

q: 20. Annual series of amounts for a period equivalent to the cash inflows and/or cash outflows, computed with deduction of expenses and capital recovery receipts is:
explain: Annual Worth (AW) converts all cash flows into an equivalent uniform annual series over the project's life.

q: 21. The benefit cost ratio is
options: is not related with discount rate
explain: As the discount rate increases, both present value of benefits and costs decrease, but generally the ratio decreases with a higher discount rate — making BCR inversely related to the discount rate.

q: 22. Net Present Value (NPV) is defined as the total present value (PV) of............of cash flows.
explain: NPV involves discounting a sequence of cash flows (a time series) back to their present value equivalents.

q: 23. In benefit-cost analysis, benefits and costs have to be converted to
explain: Benefits and costs in benefit-cost analysis can be compared using any consistent equivalent worth basis — present, future, or annual worth.

q: 24. If the investment a firm makes would ........... value from the firm, it means that NPV < 0.
explain: A negative NPV indicates that the project destroys value or 'subtracts' from the firm's net worth.

q: 25. Investment less the discounted benefit is called ......
explain: The key marks NPV, the net of discounted benefits against investment.

q: 26. The minimum value of NPV for selection of an Engineering project should be
explain: The minimum acceptable NPV for selecting an engineering project is zero, indicating the project at least breaks even.

q: 27. Which of the following has least significance in Benefit Cost Analysis of a Public Project?
options: identification of relevant benefits and costs
explain: Public projects focus on long-term social welfare (B/C ratio); the payback period is a private-sector metric focused on liquidity and is less critical for public infrastructure.

q: 28. The ratio of current assets to current liabilities is known as
explain: The current ratio is a liquidity ratio that measures a company's ability to pay short-term obligations.

q: 29. For any project to be feasible:
options: annual work should be equal to zero
payback period should be equal to less than 5 years
explain: Economic feasibility is generally defined by a positive Net Present Value (NPV) or Present Worth.

q: 30. The internal rate of return (IRR) is a rate of return used in capital budgeting to measure and compare the .......... of investments.
explain: IRR measures 'profitability' or 'efficiency'; since these terms aren't in options A, B, or C, 'none of these' is the correct choice.

q: 31. IRR is carried out for
options: evaluation the progress of the project
evaluating the desirability of investment of projects
explain: IRR is a decision-making tool to determine if an investment meets the required return threshold.

q: 32. Another name for Net Present Value (NPV) is
explain: Net Present Worth (NPW) and Net Present Value (NPV) are interchangeable terms in engineering economics.

q: 33. For selection of any project which of the following is mostly used ......
explain: Key answer d as I read it. Note: this differs from Q29 (IRR) and textbooks usually name NPV or IRR, so please verify against a clearer key.

q: 34. Project Appraisal means ......
explain: Appraisal means evaluating a proposed option and selecting the best one.

q: 35. Cost benefit study are essential to ......
options: to assess the total cost of work
ascertain the relevant went escalation in prices
evaluate viability and worthwhileness of taking up the project
explain: A cost-benefit study is carried out to decide whether the project is viable and worth undertaking.
